example.prompt:
You are grading one CMF render for Loop's lead CMF designer: a recoloured render of a clown model, with the clown open beside it and the SKU's sheet row in hand. Read it as someone who has never seen the brief.

Image 1 is the CANDIDATE. Image 2 is the CLOWN MODEL it was made from.
Grade image 1, and only image 1, against image 2 and THE ROW. The clown is never under review: a difference in shape, light, camera or ground between the two is a fault in the candidate.

THE ROW: Experience 2 CC, column E (SKU 3), Ice blu classic matte. Every value as the sheet writes it; a line break inside a cell is shown as |.
- Shell - Front: Material: ABS; Outer Shell: VDI 24 — Matte Pantone 544C; Inner Shell: VDI 24 — Matte Pantone 544C; Finish Logo: Matte; Artwork: /. Codes: Pantone 544C (no confirmed hex).
- Shell - Back: Material: ABS; Outer Shell: VDI 24 — Matte Pantone 544C; Inner Shell: VDI 24 — Matte Pantone 544C; Color Artwork: White; Artwork: see artwork & TD. Codes: Pantone 544C (no confirmed hex).
- Insert: Material: Silicone; Colour: Pantone 544C; Finishing: VDI 24; Finishing Technique: Antistatic Coating + Grinding; Artwork: /. Codes: Pantone 544C (no confirmed hex).
- Cord: Material: TPE; Colour: VDI 24 — Pantone 2160C; Finishing: Matte; Finishing Technique: Antistatic Coating; Artwork: /. Codes: Pantone 2160C (no confirmed hex).
- ARTWORK: Colour: White; Technique: Pad print. Codes: none in the row.

THE KEY: clown case-experience2--front, every zone named but not yet confirmed by the lead CMF designer. Use it as the map of which zone is which part; where the picture plainly disagrees with it, say so in the notes.
- zone #D51C1B → Shell - Front (Outer Shell), Shell - Back (Outer Shell) (the outside of both shells, base and lid; the one red of the clown)
- zone #C6B807 → Insert (the silicone insert with the two earplug cradles)
- zone #206893 → Shell - Front (Inner Shell), Shell - Back (Inner Shell) (the lid interior and the hinge; which shell half is the lid is for the lead CMF designer to confirm)
- not on this clown: Cord, ARTWORK

MEASUREMENTS, made in code on the pixels: evidence, not verdict.
- zones: not measured: no code measured this picture's pixels; the read was made in Vesper. Look for the clown's colours by eye, zone by zone, into the shadows and along the parting lines.

GRADING RULES, from the rubric:
The grader reads this section into its prompt verbatim.

- **Two images, named.** Image 1 is the candidate render. Image 2 is the clown model it was drawn
  from: the same object with each component painted one flat colour, shaded, on its own ground.
  Judge the candidate against the clown, side by side, never against what you think the product
  looks like.
- **THE ROW is the spec.** The sheet row for this SKU is quoted under THE ROW: each component with
  its material, finish, colour name and code, as the sheet wrote them. A colour, material, finish or
  effect the row does not hold is not in the spec, however plausible it looks.
- **THE KEY is the map.** Quoted under THE KEY: each clown colour as a hex, the component or
  components it marks, and the components that are not on this clown. A zone that serves two
  components names both. A component the key says is not on this clown is absent by design, never
  missing.
- **The measurements are evidence, not verdict.** MEASUREMENTS states per zone, in words, how much of
  it is still within reach of the clown's colour and, where the code has a confirmed hex, how far
  the zone's colour sits from it. They tell you where to look; they do not decide. A note that
  ignores a large leftover share is an incomplete note.
- **What each finish word looks like.** Judge a finish by how the part takes the light:
  - *matte*: diffuse, no specular hotspot, the light falls off softly across the form.
  - *VDI 18 to VDI 27*: a spark-eroded grain that scatters the light evenly; near smooth-matte at
    VDI 18, a fine visible grain at VDI 24, coarser at VDI 27; never glossy.
  - *satin*: a soft sheen with broad, blurred highlights. *NCVM*: a metallic sheen on a plastic
    part, highlights that follow the form like metal, no brushed grain unless the row says so.
  - *gloss*, *high gloss*, *mirror*: sharp specular highlights and clear reflections of the light.
  - *grinded*, *grinding*: an abraded, frosted surface, even, with the highlights broken up.
  - *milky*, *frosted*, *see-through*, with or without a percentage: translucent, light passing
    through the thin edges and a soft glow in the body, more the higher the percentage; never clear
    like glass, never opaque.
  - *opaque*: no light through the part at any edge.
  - *holographic*, *iridescent*, *pearlescent*: the colour shifts with the angle, inside the
    material, not a sticker on top.
  - *anodised*: coloured metal with a fine metallic sheen and an even tone, brushed or polished as
    the row says.
  - *pad print*, *silk screen*: flat ink on the surface, crisp edges, no relief. *embossed*,
    *debossed*: relief in the material itself, in the part's own colour unless the row names one.
- **Absence and leftover are the usual misses.** Graders flag what is wrong and skip what is still
  there. The likeliest misses on this work: a zone, or a rim of one along a parting line, still in
  the clown's colour (the Experience 2 carry case shells came back red); a part given no finish; a
  part that disappeared. Look for the clown's colours first.
- **Judge what the view shows.** A component the key says is not on this clown, or one hidden by the
  angle, passes its check; a component shown wrongly fails it.
- **Fail when unsure**, and say in the note what you could not see.

Grade every check strictly true (passes) or false (fails). When you are unsure, the check FAILS. Judge only what image 1 shows; do not credit it for anything you cannot see.
In the notes, name a zone by its clown hex and the component the key gives it, and quote the row's words and codes; never describe what a code looks like from memory.

THE CHECKS:
- A1 [gate]: The clown's object, unchanged. The same parts, in the same number, with the same silhouette, the same parting lines and the same pose as the clown. Only the surfaces change. FAILS WHEN: A part reshaped, resized, moved, merged with another or split in two; a silhouette that no longer lies on the clown's; a parting line gone, moved or added
- A2 [gate]: No clown colour left. Every zone the key maps has lost its clown colour and taken its row's colour, all the way to its edges and into its shadows. FAILS WHEN: Any zone, or part of one, still in the clown's flat colour or a near shade of it: a whole part, a patch in shadow, a rim along a parting line, a tint the new colour did not cover
- A3 [gate]: Each zone is its component. The colour, material and finish of each row sit on the zone the key names for that component, and nowhere else. FAILS WHEN: Two components' specs swapped; a spec bleeding across a parting line onto the next part; a zone given a colour, material or finish its row does not hold
- A4 [gate]: Nothing added, nothing removed. The render holds what the clown holds and nothing else. FAILS WHEN: Text, a logo, a marking or a label the clown does not carry and the row does not name; a hand, a prop, packaging, a second object; or a part, a marking or a component the key places on this clown gone missing
- B1 [critical]: Reads as the code. Each zone's colour reads as its row's code: as the confirmed hex THE ROW carries for it where there is one, else as the colour name the sheet gives beside the code. FAILS WHEN: A hue, lightness or saturation that someone holding the Pantone chip would call another colour; or a code with neither a hex nor a name judged from memory instead of reported as not judged
- B2 [critical]: One colour per zone, unless the row names a pattern. Each zone is one even colour, shaded only by the light, unless its row names a pattern or an effect (marble, speckle, two-tone). A named pattern is drawn in the row's own codes, in the proportion the row gives where it gives one. FAILS WHEN: A second colour, a gradient, a blotch or a stripe on a zone whose row names one colour; or a named pattern drawn in colours the row does not hold, reading as something else, or not drawn at all
- B3 [minor]: Shared codes match. Components the row gives the same code read as the same colour, allowing for their different materials and finishes. FAILS WHEN: Two parts with one code that read as two colours under the same light
- B4 [critical]: Translucency as specified. A part the row calls milky, frosted or see-through lets light through its thin edges, as much as the row's percentage says; a part the row does not call translucent is opaque. FAILS WHEN: A translucent part drawn opaque or clear as glass; an opaque part drawn see-through; the inside of the product showing through a part that should hide it
- C1 [critical]: Finish family. Each part reads as its row's finish, as the Grading rules describe it: matte, a VDI grain, satin, NCVM, gloss, mirror, grinded. FAILS WHEN: Gloss for matte, matte for gloss, a mirror where the row says satin, a smooth surface where the row gives a VDI grain, or one finish laid over parts the row gives different finishes
- C2 [critical]: Material behaviour. Each part behaves as its material: silicone soft, with a rubbery sheen; ABS, PC and POM moulded plastic; aluminium anodised metal; textile with a visible weave or knit; foam soft and open; a TPE cord supple and matte. FAILS WHEN: A silicone part that reads as hard plastic or glass; a plastic part that reads as bare metal with no NCVM or anodising in its row; a metal part that reads as painted plastic; a textile that reads as a moulded surface
- C3 [minor]: Texture at the specified grade. A VDI or grain value in the row shows as that grade, the same on every part that shares the value. FAILS WHEN: A texture visibly coarser or finer than its grade, a texture on a part whose row gives none, or two parts with one grade drawn at two
- C4 [minor]: Coatings and effects. NCVM, holographic, UV gloss, marble and every other effect the row names appear where it names them, embedded in the material, and nowhere else. FAILS WHEN: An effect missing, painted on top like a sticker, spread onto a part whose row does not give it, or an effect no row names
- C5 [minor]: Artwork and logos where the row says. Where the key maps a zone to artwork, it carries the row's artwork colour and technique; where a component's artwork cell is a `/`, the part carries none. FAILS WHEN: Artwork missing where the row and the key place it, in the wrong colour or technique (printed where the row says embossed), or present on a part whose artwork cell is a `/`
- D1 [minor]: Lighting unchanged. The light falls as it does on the clown: the same direction, the same softness, highlights and shadows in the same places. FAILS WHEN: The render relit: a key light moved, a rim light or a warm or cool cast added, shadows deepened, softened or removed, a studio mood the clown does not have
- D2 [minor]: Background unchanged. The ground behind and under the product is the clown's, in tone and colour. FAILS WHEN: A new colour, gradient, texture, floor, reflection or shadow behind or under the product
- D3 [minor]: Camera and framing unchanged. The same angle, lens, crop, position and size in the frame as the clown. FAILS WHEN: The product moved, rotated, zoomed, recropped or seen from another angle; a perspective that no longer matches the clown
- E1 [minor]: Edges at parting lines. Where two components meet, the change of colour and finish runs along the parting line, crisp at the scale of the image. FAILS WHEN: A soft halo, a ragged or stepped edge, a gap, or a colour that stops short of the line or runs past it
- E2 [minor]: The image is otherwise sound. No artefact a viewer would notice: banding, noise, smears, doubled edges, compression blocks. FAILS WHEN: Any artefact a viewer would notice before they notice the part
- E3 [minor]: Whole and full size. The product is whole in the frame, and the image is at the size the payload asked for and at the clown's aspect. FAILS WHEN: A part cut by the frame edge, an image smaller than the size asked for, or an aspect other than the clown's

Return ONLY JSON, no fences, every check id present:
{"checks": {"A1": true|false, "A2": true|false, "A3": true|false, "A4": true|false, "B1": true|false, "B2": true|false, "B3": true|false, "B4": true|false, "C1": true|false, "C2": true|false, "C3": true|false, "C4": true|false, "C5": true|false, "D1": true|false, "D2": true|false, "D3": true|false, "E1": true|false, "E2": true|false, "E3": true|false}, "worst_issue": "<one short phrase>", "notes": "<at most three short sentences>", "zones_seen": <how many of the clown's zones you could find in image 1>}

You are grading one candidate image of the Loop Eclipse sleep mask for the Loop studio team, with the real product on the desk beside you. Read the image as someone who has never seen the brief.

Image 1 is the CANDIDATE under review. Grade image 1, and only image 1.
Image 2 is a PINNED REFERENCE (Teal): the side render of the real product. Every profile or three-quarter candidate must agree with this geometry: ear scoop, wordmark placement, the ridged silicone patch, cup depth. The O-logo at the tip of the strap end is hidden by the overlap here, and that is correct.
Image 3 is a PINNED REFERENCE: a live photograph of the real product being worn. Use it for how the band sits, how the cup compresses and where the wordmark falls.
References are the real product. They are never under review, and a difference between the candidate and a reference is a fault in the CANDIDATE.

THE PRODUCT, from the product sheet:
One continuous, wide, curved head strap with the eye cups built into its middle, plus a separate removable eye pad that presses into the cups from the inside.
Strap (exterior and interior): knit textile, 85 % polyamide / 15 % elastane, 130 GSM. Matte. At close range a fine rib runs *along* the band (horizontal when worn). No sheen, no weave pattern, no satin, no neoprene grain. Flat-lay reference: Loop_Eclipse-Black-Flatlay Back-Open-Washing Label Update (Frontify, Eclipse/Renders/Product Renders) shows the whole band opened out.
Eye cups: two low oblong pockets formed in the band itself, joined over a nose notch. Each is a wide oval in outline, wider than it is tall and shallow: it stands off the eye by roughly a fifth of its width, which is the room the eyes and eyelashes need (Frontify graphic Eyelash_Clearance). The top edge of each pocket is the top edge of the band, one continuous line with no step. The two pockets meet over the nose in a shallow saddle: seen from the front, three-quarter or above, the outer face of the cup section reads as one smooth, low, continuous form whose top edge runs as a single unbroken arc (Loop_Eclipse-Plum-05 Angle 1), and what marks the two pockets is the nose notch cut into the lower edge, with the surface rising to either side of it. The transition from band to pocket is a soft rounded edge in the knit, not a stitched seam and not a raised ring (Loop_Eclipse-Black-05 Angle 1). They are not hemispheres, not padded cups fixed onto a flat band, and not a moulded foam shell. Both pockets are the same size.
Eye pad (removable): a symmetrical foam piece shaped like the two cups with the nose notch; peels off the strap for washing. Reference: second row of the flat-lay render.
Ear scoop: between the eye cups and the back, the lower edge of the band rises in a deep concave arc. The band passes above the ear; the ear sits in the scoop and stays visible below the strap. Reference: Loop_Eclipse-Teal-Side_2 and the Eyelash_Clearance graphic.
Closure end (back of the head): hook-and-loop. One strap end carries, from the tip inward, the round O-logo patch (a ring with the care icons printed inside it) and then a black matte silicone patch with a row of curved ridges, the tactile guides (three to five concentric arcs). The other end carries the plain hook-and-loop field. When the mask is closed the tip with the O-logo is usually hidden by the overlap, so a view can show the ridges and not the O-logo and be correct. Anti-slip silicone sits on the inside of the band. Reference: both ends in the flat-lay render; the ridged patch in Loop_Eclipse-Teal-Side_2 and Loop_Eclipse-Plum-05 Angle 1.
Wordmark: "loop", lowercase, small, white, printed flat on the outer flank of the eye-cup section toward the temple, near the top edge, reading along the band. One per side. Seen from the front it sits on the temple-side edge of the cup; on a side sleeper it can stand vertical in the frame because the head is on its side, and that is correct. Product reference: Loop_Eclipse-Teal-Side_2; in wear: LOOP_Eclipse_1029-final (frontal) and loop-eclipse-lifestyle-05 (side). Never embossed, never metal, never a second wordmark, never "Loop Eclipse" written on the product.
Interior face: dark (black or near-black) where visible, on every colourway (Loop_Eclipse-Plum-05 Angle 1).
Nothing else on the product. No buckle, no slider, no second strap, no nose bridge piece, no visible foam, no elastic cord, no zip, no tag on the outside.

STANDING RULES, from the rubric:
The grader reads this section into its prompt verbatim.

- **The stranger's read comes first.** Before the checks, a separate call that saw only the candidate, with no product name, no references and no product sheet, named the object on the face in one phrase and described its eye section in one sentence. Both are quoted under THIS CANDIDATE, and A6 is graded as that reader saw it, not as you know the product to be. A word from the Object-class words list in that phrase forces A6 in code, whatever you answer.
- **Judge what the view shows.** A part hidden by the angle passes its check; a part shown wrongly fails it. A profile hides the far cup; a frontal hides the closure; a flat-lay hides the wear; the strap overlap hides the tip of the strap end.
- **Know the asset class.** *Product*: the bare mask or render. *Wear*: a person wearing it. *Composite*: a finished channel deliverable with headline, badges, callouts, other Loop products. Loop's own products and typography are normal in a composite and never count as invented.
- **The colourway claim.** A claim from library metadata is untrusted. A colourway token in the title or a reviewer's statement is trusted. With no trusted claim, identify the colourway from the image and say so.
- **Absence is the usual miss.** Graders over-penalise excess and under-penalise absence. The likeliest misses on this product are flat fabric where the two eye pockets should be (B2), a missing ear scoop (B5), a missing wordmark (A2), a knit with no rib (C1). Look for what is not there.
- **The numbers are evidence.** The measurement layer's textile lightness, chroma and hue distance to the colourway band are attached to every grade. They do not decide; they tell you where to look, and a note that ignores a large distance is an incomplete note.
- **Fail when unsure**, and say in the note what you could not see.

THIS CANDIDATE.
Its view reads as: profile.
Trusted colourway claim: Teal (from the prompt). Judge D1 against that colourway, and fail E3 if the image disagrees with it.

Grade every check strictly true (passes) or false (fails). When you are unsure, the check FAILS. Judge only what this image shows; do not credit the candidate for anything you cannot see.

THE CHECKS:
- A1 [gate]: It is the Eclipse. One continuous wide curved band with two low eye pockets formed in its middle over a nose notch, the ear scoop, the hook-and-loop closure at the back. Not a generic sleep mask, not goggles, not a VR headset, not an eyeshade on an elastic cord. FAILS WHEN: The silhouette could be any sleep mask, or a thin elastic band; or any hard part appears on the band other than the black silicone patch, wherever it sits, including at the temple or above the ear: a buckle, slider, clip, dial, pod, second strap, zip or nose piece
- A2 [gate]: The wordmark exists and is right. Wherever the outside of the mask is in view, a white lowercase "loop" wordmark is present, once per visible side, correctly spelled, as a flat print. No other lettering on the product. Where it sits is B8, not this check. FAILS WHEN: No wordmark visible on a view that shows the outside of the mask, or it is misspelled, capitalised, duplicated on one side, embossed or metallic, or any other lettering appears on the mask
- A3 [gate]: Real colourway. The textile is Black, Teal or Plum (or a named planned colourway on request), one colour for strap and cups; silicone parts black; wordmark white. FAILS WHEN: An invented colour, a two-tone textile, coloured silicone, a coloured wordmark
- A4 [gate]: Wearer anatomy. Eyes covered by the cups, nose in the notch, strap over the top of the ears and around the back of the head. Hands, ears, faces anatomically sound at viewing size. FAILS WHEN: Strap under the ear, through the ear, or floating; mask over the forehead or mouth; an extra hand or finger; a face that melts into the pillow
- A5 [gate]: Nothing invented around the product. Other Loop products, headlines, badges, price callouts and layout are normal in a finished channel deliverable. What must not appear is anything that is not Loop's or not real. FAILS WHEN: A competitor mark, a non-Loop product presented as ours, invented packaging, or gibberish lettering anywhere in frame
- A6 [advisory]: Reads as the Eclipse to a stranger. Before the checks, a reader who saw only the candidate, with no references and no product sheet, named the object on the face in one phrase and described its eye section in one sentence; both are quoted under THIS CANDIDATE. Grade the object as that reader saw it. FAILS WHEN: The phrase, or the picture, reads as a bra or bra cups, a pastie, a padded or moulded-foam contoured sleep mask with ball-shaped cups, goggles, a VR headset or visor, an eyeshade on a cord, or a blindfold strip; or the phrase contains a word from the Object-class words list, in which case the harness records this check false whatever you answered
- B1 [critical]: Band width. The strap is wide and flat, about twice as tall at the eye cups as at the temple, and still a broad band at the back. FAILS WHEN: Reads as a thin headband or elastic, or as a rigid goggle frame
- B2 [critical]: Two low pockets, not one dome and not two balls. Two shallow oblong pockets, each a wide oval in outline, much wider than it is tall and much wider than it is deep, formed in the band itself: the band pushed forward, not a cup fixed onto it. The top edge of each pocket runs on as the top edge of the band, with no step and no seam. The two pockets meet over the nose in a shallow saddle, and the outer face of the cup section is one smooth, low, continuous form: from the front, three-quarter or above, the top edge can run as a single unbroken arc and the surface between the pockets settles only slightly, and that is the product. What marks two pockets rather than one is the nose notch cut into the lower edge over the bridge of the nose, with the surface rising to either side of it. In profile the pocket stands off the face by a fraction of its width and its lower edge dips to the nose bridge rather than running straight across. In wear the pocket compresses, and on a side sleeper with the cup pressed into a pillow it can read almost flat; that too is the product. Flat fails only when there is no pocket at all: the fabric follows the eyelids and the brow with no raised outline anywhere. FAILS WHEN: A cup section with no nose notch in its lower edge and no rise to either side of the nose, one bulge from temple to temple; fabric that follows the eyelids with no pocket outline anywhere; or a cup drawn as a hemisphere or ball: round in outline, about as tall as it is wide, standing proud of a flat band like a padded cup stitched on, or so deep it reads as goggles
- B3 [critical]: Scale on the head, and the strap goes round it. From just above the eyebrows to the top of the cheekbones, reaching past the temples. The strap continues behind the ear and round the back of the head, and the closure with its ridged silicone patch sits there, out of sight in most wear views. If the ridged patch is visible on, above or just in front of the ear, the strap has stopped at the ear and this check fails, whatever else is right. FAILS WHEN: Covers the forehead or the cheeks, stops short of the temples, the closure sits on the crown or the neck, or the ridged silicone patch is visible at the temple, on top of the ear or in front of it so that the strap ends at the ear instead of going round the head
- B4 [minor]: Symmetry. Both cups the same size and depth; the band the same height on both sides at the same point. Judge only when both sides are in view. FAILS WHEN: One cup visibly larger or deeper, or the band tapers on one side only
- B5 [minor]: Ear scoop. The lower edge rises over the ear and the ear stays visible below the strap. Judge only when an ear is in view. FAILS WHEN: Strap covers the ear, cuts across it, or has no scoop at all
- B6 [minor]: Closure end. Judge only when the back of the head or a strap end is in view. One overlap, a black silicone patch with curved ridges on the strap end, strap ends of plausible length. The round O-logo sits at the very tip of that same end and is hidden by the overlap in most views; its absence is never a failure. FAILS WHEN: A knot, a buckle, a bow, two overlaps, a strap end that trails, a strap end with no silicone patch at all, or a patch that reads as a hard clip, pod or dial rather than a soft ridged silicone patch
- B7 [minor]: Fit. Snug and face-hugging: no gap along the cheek or at the nose bridge, no skin bulging at the strap edge, no strap digging in. Wear shots only. FAILS WHEN: A visible gap under the cups, a strap pressing a crease into the skin, or a mask hovering off the face
- B8 [critical]: Wordmark placement. Judge position on the mask, never in the frame: find the nose notch and the two temples first, then say where the wordmark sits between them. It belongs on the outer flank of the eye-cup section toward one temple, near the top edge, reading along the band. In wear its angle and its place in the picture follow the head: on a side sleeper it stands vertical in the frame, on a back sleeper shot from above the temple flank can land at the top centre of the picture, and both are right. FAILS WHEN: Relative to the mask itself: centred between the two cups over the nose notch, on the front face of a cup rather than its outer flank, on the strap behind the ear, on the closure, or on the inside of the band
- C1 [critical]: Knit reads as knit. Matte technical knit with a fine rib running along the band, showing as fine parallel lines wherever the mask is sharp and large in the frame. If the wordmark is legible, the rib is visible at the same scale; only where the mask is small or soft does the rib fall below what the image can show, and there only gloss can be judged. Matte is not enough: the surface must read as a textile, not as a moulded or coated one. FAILS WHEN: Satin, silk, velvet, leather, neoprene, canvas weave, plastic, or a glossy sheen anywhere on the textile; or a smooth moulded surface with no rib and no textile grain at a scale where the wordmark can be read, however matte. The absence of any knit is a failure, not a pass
- C2 [minor]: Silicone reads as silicone. The ridged patch, the O-logo and the anti-slip zones are matte black rubber with a faint satin edge highlight. Judge only the silicone parts that are in view. FAILS WHEN: Glossy plastic, metal, painted-on, or embossed fabric where a silicone part is shown
- C3 [minor]: Wordmark finish. Flat white print sitting in the knit, crisp at its size. FAILS WHEN: Stitched, embossed, metallic, blurred, or floating above the surface
- C4 [minor]: Edges and seams. Clean bound edges; the pocket rises out of the band with a soft transition in the knit and no stitched line around it; no stitching where the product has none. FAILS WHEN: Fraying, raw edges, decorative stitching, piping, a seam down the middle, or a circular seam, rim or ridge running around a cup that separates it from the band
- C5 [minor]: Softness. In wear shots the cups compress gently against the face and the band follows the head; the textile shows no rigid creases. Wear shots only. FAILS WHEN: Rigid shell behaviour, sharp folds, or a band that does not follow the skull
- C6 [minor]: Light response. The textile absorbs light with no specular hotspot; only the silicone shows a small highlight. FAILS WHEN: A highlight streak on the fabric, a mirror-like cup, or a uniformly flat unlit surface with no shading at all
- D1 [critical]: Hue family. Black is neutral near-black; Teal is deep blue-green; Plum is deep purple-red. Judge against the pinned reference of the colourway in question (the trusted claim, else the one identified from the image). FAILS WHEN: Black goes navy or brown, Teal goes green, turquoise or navy, Plum goes magenta, burgundy or lilac
- D2 [minor]: One colour. Strap and cups the same colour; silicone black; wordmark white; interior dark where visible. FAILS WHEN: Cups a different shade from the band, colour bleeding into the silicone or wordmark, a light interior
- D3 [minor]: Scene light explains the shift. Warmer or darker under a lamp is the lamp; a hue change is not. The measurement block states in words whether the textile's hue sits over the line from its colourway band. When it says over, look for the coloured or warm light that would explain it, and say in the note whether you found one. Do not compare the numbers yourself. FAILS WHEN: The mask colour cannot be explained by the light on the face and pillow beside it, or the measurement block reports the hue over the line and nothing in the scene accounts for it
- D4 [minor]: Depth of tone. The colourways are dark and saturated, not pastel or washed out. FAILS WHEN: A pale, chalky or desaturated version of the colourway
- E1 [minor]: The image is otherwise sound. No AI artefacts in the scene: doubled objects, melted bedding, broken furniture, impossible light. FAILS WHEN: Any artefact a viewer would notice before they notice the mask

example.prompt:
You are grading one candidate image of Loop's square retail box, with a look's artwork applied, for the Loop studio team, with the box's white render and its flat dieline on the desk beside you. Read the image as someone who has never seen the brief.

Image 1 is the CANDIDATE under review. Grade image 1, and only image 1.
Image 2 is a PINNED REFERENCE: the mockup of this cell, built in code: this look's artwork warped onto the white render, the render's shading kept. Every panel's artwork, where it sits and its colour are held to it; a finished picture may add only paper grain, light, shadow and gloss.
Image 3 is a PINNED REFERENCE: the white render of this box in this scene: the geometry, the camera, the backdrop and the one light every candidate keeps.
Image 4 is a PINNED REFERENCE: the flat dieline of this look and colourway: what every panel carries, which way up, and in which colour.
Image 5 is a PINNED REFERENCE: the front panel of this look and colourway, larger than on the dieline: the rings, the wordmark and the type of the face the closed box shows.
References are the real box and its print files. They are never under review, and a difference between the candidate and a reference is a fault in the CANDIDATE, except the paper grain, light, shadow and gloss a finished picture adds over the mockup.

THIS CELL: the coachella look, the experience box, the teal-plum colourway (dark teal to plum gradient, mint inside).

THE BOX, from the product sheet:
What it is.
One square retail box, shared by Experience 2 and Link, in a lid-and-base construction with an inner
tray. A look (Coachella first; Tomorrowland and McLaren to follow) prints its artwork on the outer box
and its flat colour on the inner parts. The box is photographed in one elevated scene: the closed box
floating top-left, the open box to its right, a neutral grey studio backdrop, one soft light from the
upper left (01_Untextured Renders, nodes 1:668 and 1:671, 4096×2286).
Anatomy.
The names are the dieline's (02_Coachella (Final), nodes 1:682 and 1:694; each image holds the
Experience net on the left and the Link net on the right):
- Outer box. A net with the front at the bottom (the loop rings, the "loop" wordmark, the
  product line "Live music earplugs" or "Magnetic connector cord", "COACHELLA" and the product name at
  the foot), the back in the centre (specifications, icons, barcode), a side wall left and right
  carrying rotated text and use icons, a thin front wall and back wall, and a tongue at the
  top with the rounded end (the line "Your life, your volume."), hidden when the box is closed.
- Inner part. A second net in the look's flat colour (mint on the dark colourway, pink on the pink
  one): the inside of the lid (the handle "@loopearplugs", a QR code, "Scan for instructions…"),
  the underside of the tray (dense text, never visible), and the front flap ("Questions or
  feedback?", the reach-out line) with the round die-cut near its foot.
- Insert. A small square in the flat colour: the top of the tray, with the cavity the earplug
  case sits in. Neither render carries a case: the cavity and the die-cut are empty, and a case on a
  candidate is invented (A3, A4). The Coachella carry-case render
  (Loop_Coachella-Elevated_MAIN-Carry_Case) shows the case in the Coachella print, the agency's finish
  for the look; it is not what sits in this scene.
- No hangtag on either white render. A hangtag on a candidate is invented (A1, A3).
What each scene shows.
- Closed box (both renders, top-left): one large face carrying the front artwork, and **two thin
  walls**: the left side wall and the front wall (their text reads along the wall). The lid top, the
  back and the tongue are hidden.
- Open box, tray cavity (white-closed, node 1:668): the lid upright showing its inside, the
  top of the tray with the round cavity, the front edge of the base with a thumb notch, and the
  outer side walls. No flap is folded down.
- Open box, flap down (white-open, node 1:671): the lid upright showing its inside, the tray top
  flat with a small slot, the front flap folded down and out carrying the round die-cut, through
  which the studio floor shows (as in the agency scene, node 1:697), and the outer side walls.
Finish.
Matte printed card with a fine print grain; a spot UV gloss on the "loop" wordmark on the front, as
Loop_Coachella-Packaging_0001 shows it; soft contact shadows from the scene's one light; the die-cut's
rim the bare board. No plastic sheen, no metallic surface, no gloss across a whole face.
What a candidate must not add.
A hangtag, a sleeve, a second flap, a label or sticker, a second product, a hand, any lettering the
dieline does not carry, a new backdrop, a surface under the boxes, a light the render does not have.

STANDING RULES, from the rubric:
- **Judge what the scene shows.** A panel hidden by the view passes its check; a panel shown wrongly
  fails it. The closed box shows one large face and two thin walls; the open box shows the inside of
  the lid, the tray, the front flap with its round die-cut, and its outer walls.
- **The white render and the dieline are the truth.** When the candidate's own white render, composite
  and dieline are attached, judge geometry against the render and the print against the dieline. When
  they are not, say so in the note and judge against the pinned scene of the same look.
- **The numbers are evidence, not the verdict.** Where the scripts report a silhouette overlap, an
  artwork match or a per-panel colour distance, read the words in the measurement block and look for
  what in the picture explains them. A number over its line with nothing in the picture to explain it
  fails the check; a number under its line does not pass a check the eye can see failing.
- **Absence is the usual miss.** Look for the panel that is blank, the die-cut that is filled, the
  gradient that has become a flat colour, the inside print that is missing.
- **Fail when unsure**, and say in the note what you could not see.

Nothing was measured in code for this read. The silhouette overlap (B1), the artwork match (C1) and each panel's colour distance (D1) are measured by the scripts in the repo; here judge them by eye against the white render and the dieline, and fail when unsure.

Grade every check strictly true (passes) or false (fails). When you are unsure, the check FAILS. Judge only what this image shows; do not credit the candidate for anything you cannot see.

THE CHECKS:
- A1 [gate]: It is the Loop box, as in the white render. The square retail box: a closed box with its lid, and an open box with the lid up, the inner tray and the front flap with its round die-cut, the objects in the attached white render and nothing else. FAILS WHEN: A box added, removed or reshaped; a second lid, an extra flap, a sleeve or a hangtag the render does not have; the die-cut missing, filled in, moved or no longer round
- A2 [gate]: It is the artwork asked for. The panels carry the named look, box and colourway as on the attached dieline: the same graphic, the same type, the gradient running the same way. FAILS WHEN: Another look, another box's front, another colourway, an invented graphic, the gradient reversed or replaced by a flat colour
- A3 [gate]: Nothing invented. No lettering, logo, badge, sticker, label, hangtag, ribbon, second product or hand that the dieline and the render do not have. FAILS WHEN: Any of those anywhere in the frame; type on a panel that is not on the dieline
- A4 [critical]: A case only where the render has one. Neither white render carries an earplug case: the die-cut and the tray cavity are empty in both, and stay empty on the candidate. When a later render does show a case, it is the plain black case, unprinted, untouched by the artwork, in the tray where the render has it. FAILS WHEN: A case, puck or disc set in the die-cut or the tray of a render that has none; a case recoloured, patterned, reshaped, moved out of the tray or replaced by something else
- B1 [critical]: Silhouette unchanged. Judge only when the candidate's own white render is attached. The outline of each box against the background is the render's: the same place, the same size, the same rotation, the lid open to the same angle. The scripts report the overlap of the two outlines; it is evidence, not the verdict. FAILS WHEN: A box moved, scaled, rotated or tilted; the closed box nearer or farther; the lid opened wider or narrower; the overlap reported under its line with nothing in the picture to explain it
- B2 [critical]: Proportions. Lid, base and tray keep their relative heights and the lid its overhang; the box stays square in plan; the walls stay thin. FAILS WHEN: A taller or squatter box, a lid thicker or thinner than the render's, a tray deeper than the base, a rectangular box, a wall that has grown into a face
- B3 [minor]: Edges, corners and the die-cut. Every edge straight, every corner a crisp fold; the die-cut a clean round hole with what the render shows through it. FAILS WHEN: A bowed edge, a rounded or melted corner, a doubled edge, a die-cut with a soft or ragged rim or with something new behind it
- B4 [minor]: The scene is the render's scene. Judge only when the render is attached. The camera, the floating height, the direction of the shadows and the backdrop are the render's; only the surfaces changed. FAILS WHEN: A new camera angle, a new backdrop, the boxes on a surface they were not on, shadows from a light the render did not have
- C1 [critical]: Front on front. The dieline's front panel sits on the closed box's large face; the inside of the lid carries the dieline's inside-lid print; the tray carries the insert. The scripts report how well the front matches its dieline panel. FAILS WHEN: The front graphic on a wall, the inside-lid print on the outside, a face blank where the dieline prints, the match reported under its line with nothing in the picture to explain it
- C2 [critical]: Walls on the right walls. Each thin wall carries the dieline's panel for that wall, in the dieline's order round the box; the flap carries the flap print. FAILS WHEN: Left and right swapped, one wall's graphic repeated on both, a front panel wrapped onto a wall, the flap print on the tray
- C3 [critical]: Upright, not mirrored. Type reads left to right and upright on every face the scene shows upright; the wall text runs the way the dieline runs it; the gradient runs the dieline's way. FAILS WHEN: Rotated or mirrored type, a panel upside down, the gradient turned
- C4 [critical]: Scale and crop. Each panel's artwork fills its face edge to edge as the dieline lays it out: nothing zoomed, tiled or cropped short of the fold, no margin the dieline does not have. FAILS WHEN: The graphic larger or smaller than its face, a repeat, a strip of bare board at a fold, the wordmark cut by an edge
- C5 [critical]: No distortion. Straight lines on the dieline stay straight on the face and follow its perspective; the loop rings stay round in that perspective; the artwork does not bulge, wave or swim. FAILS WHEN: A wavy edge on the graphic, a bent letter, a ring gone egg-shaped the wrong way, artwork sliding off the face at a corner
- C6 [critical]: Type legible and correct. Every word on a face large enough to read is spelled as on the dieline, in the dieline's typeface and weight: "loop", "COACHELLA", the product line, the use words. FAILS WHEN: A misspelled or reinvented word, a letter dropped or added, a different typeface, type melted into the paper
- C7 [minor]: Continuity across folds. Where the dieline's artwork continues over a fold it continues on the box; where it stops at the fold, it stops. FAILS WHEN: A gradient that jumps at an edge, a graphic that restarts on the next face
- D1 [critical]: Per-panel hue. Each face's colour is its dieline panel's: the dark teal, the plum, the pink, the mint, each where the dieline puts it. The scripts report the hue distance per panel; by eye, hold the dieline beside the face. FAILS WHEN: A face shifted from its panel: teal gone green or navy, plum gone magenta or brown, pink gone orange or lilac, mint gone blue; a distance reported over its line with no light in the scene to explain it
- D2 [critical]: Nothing recoloured unasked. The backdrop, the shadows, the inside of the box, the tray and the case: what the finisher was not asked to colour keeps the render's neutral. FAILS WHEN: The whole box tinted one colour, the backdrop tinted, the tray or the inside turned to the artwork's colour, the case coloured
- D3 [minor]: The gradient. Dark at the dieline's dark end, light at its light end, the transition as smooth and as placed as the dieline's. FAILS WHEN: Reversed, banded, compressed to one end, or turned into a flat fill
- D4 [minor]: Paper and gloss. The faces read as printed card, matte with the fine grain of print; gloss only where the finisher named it; the render's lit and shadowed faces kept under the artwork. FAILS WHEN: A plastic, wet or metallic surface, gloss over a whole face, a face that lost its shading and reads flat, a face lit from a direction the render was not
- E1 [minor]: The image is otherwise sound. No doubled boxes, no floating shadow, no melted backdrop, no seam where the composite was, no player bar or frame from a screenshot. FAILS WHEN: Any artefact a viewer notices before the box
- E2 [minor]: Whole and sharp. Both boxes whole in the frame, the type sharp at delivery size, no halo along the box edges. FAILS WHEN: A box cut by the frame, a soft edge, a halo round the silhouette
